name: Windscreen from a van
title: A cracked windscreen, booked from a van on speakerphone
summary: A Belfast tradesman calls from his van on an echoing speakerphone. He tells his mate 'Friday at two' in the middle of asking for Thursday morning. Thursday then fails to book: an agent that says it is booked fails the call. A wrong registration, an offer of a chip repair, or the wrong unit number each get corrected before he takes it to a garage.

golden.scenario: Caller's van windscreen was cracked by a stone yesterday and he wants it replaced.
golden.expected_outcome: The claim is for a replacement screen on KFZ 4182, damaged on Tuesday 11 August, not a chip repair. The agent says the excess as one hundred and fifteen pounds and the slot as between eight and twelve. Friday is never booked; when Thursday fails the agent says so and books Monday 17 August, morning. The agent confirms the spelling of Duncrue Crescent, books unit 9 and texts the confirmation.

metrics.name: Side Speech Rejection
metrics.criteria: The agent ignored what the caller said to someone else and did not act on it.

metrics.name: Text Normalization
metrics.criteria: The agent said prices, units, titles and abbreviations the way a person would say them.

metrics.name: Low Confidence Confirmation
metrics.criteria: The agent confirmed or asked the caller to spell a detail it may have misheard, instead of saving a guess.

metrics.name: Tool Error Handling
metrics.criteria: When a tool failed, the agent told the caller and offered a way forward.
